english_title: Fabián Eduardo Sarmiento Valbuena — recorded rebuttal to reports and allegations about intelligence and reward payments
purpose: This recorded supplementary submission, submitted on 22 July 2021, responds to human-rights organizations’ reports supplied after Sarmiento’s November 2020 appearance. Reading from a document prepared with counsel, he challenges descriptions of his role, allegations about weapons and intelligence, and the meaning attributed to his reward-payment signatures.
named_people_roles: Fabián Eduardo Sarmiento Valbuena identifies himself as Brigade 16 intelligence officer during 2007; Luis Alfonso Abella Abella helped prepare the submission. It is addressed to Óscar Parra Vera. Sarmiento contests statements attributed to Marco Fabián García Céspedes and reports by the Committee in Solidarity with Political Prisoners and José Hilario López of Dignidad Humana. Sergeant Luna Camacho is central to his explanation of reserved-funds administration. Torres Escalante, Peña Chivatá, Olivera Arrieta, Faiber Amaya and Casallas appear as commanders or witnesses whose accounts he discusses.
main_accounts_claims: Sarmiento argues that references to “B2” wrongly conflate the intelligence office, its several staff members and himself personally, and that a table incorrectly assigns him operations responsibilities. He denies supplying weapons for Daniel Torres and Roque Julio Torres’s deaths, cites alleged changes in García’s accounts, and says the intelligence linking the victims to an armed group originated with DAS. He rejects interpreting reward-payment signatures as an agreement to disguise killings. Instead, he describes sequential administrative approval based on subordinate certification and alleges that irregularities concerned diversion of funds. For Las Tapias, he says he was away from Yopal and that the ordinary-justice proceedings against him were closed; he objects that the report repeats allegations despite a later correction. Discussing the Heredia Monroy and Castro Zorro case, he accepts appearing on payment documentation but attributes preparation, withdrawal and distribution to Luna Camacho. He quotes informants and a soldier who allegedly received much less money than recorded or denied providing information. He asks that these discrepancies be investigated through the underlying files and the administrator’s evidence, rather than treated as proof of his involvement in the killings.
stated_positions_responses: The submission is a sustained denial of criminal participation and a challenge to what Sarmiento regards as selective use of evidence. He says he learned of unlawful operations only through later investigations. He presents administrative delegation and distinctions between intelligence and operations as central to his position, while demanding individualized proof for allegations against him.
outcome_open_questions: He offers the recording and accompanying document as his response under the order authorizing an extension. He calls for closer examination of administrative payments and witness contradictions. The source contains no live questioning, response by the report authors or ruling resolving his objections.

english_title: Mauricio Mojica Flórez, 12 August 2021: sworn account of complaints received by the Casanare Ombudsman’s Office
purpose: This sworn declaration seeks institutional and contextual evidence from Mojica’s work at the Defensoría del Pueblo in Casanare. It examines civilian complaints, referrals to investigators, responses by military commanders and the practical obstacles to documenting suspected deaths falsely reported as combat.
named_people_roles: Mauricio Mojica Flórez speaks as a longstanding Defensoría official and former regional or sectional head, not as a military participant confessing to killings. The transcript identifies the judicial questioner as JPCC and a Procuraduría questioner as CGRM. Mojica discusses Brigade XVI, GAULA and DAS officials, largely without reliably recalling individual names. He identifies prosecutor Rodolfo Leal Galindo in an account of strained relations over threats against him, and tentatively recalls military judge Oscar Quinchía. Martín Llanos and the Bloque Centauros appear in his regional-conflict account.
main_accounts_claims: Mojica describes the conflict between paramilitary groups and a subsequent increase in reported Army combat deaths after the 2005 demobilizations. He says families and local organizations repeatedly complained that soldiers removed people from homes, farms or social gatherings and that they appeared dead in supposed combat days later. He distinguishes this recurring complaint pattern from direct knowledge of each killing. He describes receiving reports through visits and a widely circulated institutional telephone, checking with communities, notifying national Defensoría offices, requesting military explanations and forwarding inadequate or unanswered responses to prosecutors. He recalls disputes at security councils over incompatible operational claims, the stigmatization of entire municipalities as guerrilla territory and alleged forensic inconsistencies reported to his office. He says local families often identified perpetrators only as the Army, limiting unit-level attribution. He criticizes the initially limited visible investigative response but says arrests involving GAULA and DAS later changed expectations. On mass arrests, he explains that travel authorization and distance often meant he arrived after the operation, and therefore cannot reliably identify which prosecutors participated.
stated_positions_responses: He presents his role as defending civilians and reporting complaints while acknowledging that he lacked coercive power and often worked with very few staff. He describes friction with commanders and personal threats but also cooperative relations with some prosecutors. He repeatedly qualifies names, dates and institutional conclusions as uncertain, and refuses to claim knowledge of disciplinary investigations he did not follow.
outcome_open_questions: The declaration ends at 11:44. Mojica remains available to assist, but emphasizes that contemporary reports are more reliable for individual names and dates than his present memory. The testimony points toward complaint registers, referral correspondence, forensic communications and security-council records for corroboration; it does not resolve responsibility for individual deaths.

english_title: Rodolfo Leal Galindo, 12 and 20 August 2021: sworn testimony on GAULA prosecution, institutional controls and disputed knowledge
purpose: This file combines two sessions of a sworn declaration about Leal’s work as prosecutor delegated to GAULA Casanare. The questions examine operational oversight, complaints and evidence handling, and confront his account of limited knowledge with statements alleging awareness of or presence at particular operations.
named_people_roles: Rodolfo Leal Galindo identifies himself as Fifth Specialized Prosecutor delegated to GAULA Casanare, with a period in another specialized prosecution post. Martín Antonio Moreno San Juan presides. Carmen Johana Restrepo Medina participates for the Procuraduría on August 12, and Juliana Cortes Guerra is identified in the August 20 continuation. Leal discusses GAULA commanders Camargo and Soto Bracamonte, Brigade XVI commander Torres Escalante and DAS director Orlando Rivas Tovar. He singles out DAS investigators Álvaro Rojas Manjarrez, Gabriel Flórez and Daniel Sánchez in his allegations, while distinguishing them from other DAS and CTI personnel.
main_accounts_claims: Leal describes separate military, prosecutorial and judicial-police functions, but says administrative dependence and poorly controlled access complicated oversight. He alleges irregular behavior by particular DAS investigators, says he reported concerns and requested personnel changes, and argues that some activities later bypassed his office through a smaller DAS-linked arrangement. He criticizes former practices of inspecting bodies within military premises, leaving seized material with the unit reporting the death and automatically forwarding matters to military justice. He says some complaints reached him only after an operation had already produced a death, with separate homicide proceedings underway. In the continuation, questioning tests what he knew and what more he did to prevent repeated unverified operations. Confronted with allegations that he was present when Albeiro Alonso Solís Vives died, he expressly denies attending, acknowledges knowing about the planned delivery operation and says he requested another prosecutor to inspect the body afterward. He identifies potential documentary trails in military, DAS and funding reports. He also describes later changes to entry controls, displays of operational results and evidence custody.
stated_positions_responses: Leal presents himself as having challenged irregularities rather than authorized them, and stresses the limits of his jurisdiction and information. The magistrate and Procuraduría press him on that distinction, the repeated pattern of deaths and his supervisory responsibilities. He distinguishes personally observed administrative practices from inferred command knowledge and from incident details learned later; his denials remain contested testimony.
outcome_open_questions: The August 12 session is suspended at 16:01 for urgent prosecutorial duties and resumes on August 20 at 08:07, closing at 11:11. No responsibility finding is made. His account points to complaints, transfer requests, judgments, radiograms and investigation files for comparison with other witnesses and assessment of what officials knew and did.

english_title: NRAS, 28 October 2021: sworn account of coercion as a minor and the killings of Chivas and Edilson Mendoza Soto
purpose: The court receives a sworn declaration about killings in Tauramena and the circumstances in which NRAS became involved while underage. It specifically examines vulnerability, coercion, threats and later investigative treatment, after explaining her rights and obtaining her express waiver of protection against self-incrimination.
named_people_roles: NRAS is the protected declarant and describes being a minor and pregnant during the relevant events. Óscar Parra Vera presides; Sandra Lucía Yepes Arroyabe and Carmen Yohana Restrepo Medina participate for the Procuraduría. NRAS identifies soldier Wilfrido Domínguez as the principal person who threatened and directed her. César Augusto Cómbita Eslava appears as a former boyfriend, but she expressly limits what she knows about his alleged offenses. The two principal victims are José Rubiel Llanos, known as Chivas, and Edilson Mendoza Soto, known as Pipe. NRAS and the source’s XYZ label are retained without expanding the protected identity.
main_accounts_claims: NRAS describes social contact with military personnel becoming demands to identify local people and help bring them to soldiers. She says Domínguez threatened her and her relatives when she resisted. In the Chivas account, she admits enticing her friend to a supposed party under assurances that soldiers only wanted to speak with him. She says soldiers seized him, Domínguez shot him and material was placed on him; she describes an unwanted payment and threats to remain silent. She also recalls derogatory remarks by Domínguez about gay people, while distinguishing those remarks from her own view of her friend. For the second incident, she says Domínguez removed her from hospital while she was pregnant and forced her to arrange a meeting with Edilson Mendoza Soto. She says she already knew he would be killed, but believed refusal would expose her relatives to harm. She describes an ambush and subsequent staging of the victim’s possessions. She later alleges pressure during military-associated interviews, signatures on blank pages and repeated threats after providing evidence. Other allegations, including who killed a civilian intermediary, are explicitly based on inference or rumors rather than her direct observation.
stated_positions_responses: She says she did not want the victims harmed, acted under threats and has felt victimized by these events. She nevertheless expresses sorrow and asks the families for forgiveness for her involvement. The magistrate emphasizes her age and vulnerability, offers psychosocial support and states that her account must be compared with other evidence. She disclaims detailed knowledge of Cómbita’s alleged offenses.
outcome_open_questions: The declaration closes at 12:04. The court records her assertion of victimization and says further procedural questions and assessment of vulnerability remain for another stage. No responsibility finding or recognition decision is made in this session. The alleged coercion, later threats, interview practices and disputed accounts of the two operations require corroboration.

english_title: Jorge Adalberto Páez Ladino — sworn testimony on the National GAULA Directorate, 7 December 2021
purpose: To receive witness testimony about the National GAULA Directorate’s organization, statistics, funding and relationship with field units, and test whether its documentary practices and performance comparisons illuminate the Casanare events investigated in Case 03.
named_people_roles: Former Colonel Jorge Adalberto Páez Ladino testifies as a former national director of military GAULA groups. He appears without counsel after the court explains that this is sworn witness testimony rather than a proceeding accusing him of specific conduct. Judicial questioners, including Óscar Parra Vera at closing, and victims’ representatives participate. Páez describes reporting to General Freddy Padilla and interacting with ministry, FONDELIBERTAD, prosecutorial and DAS officials. Gustavo Soto Bracamonte is the source of a document shown to him; German Enciso and Humberto Velázquez are identified as officials who could clarify procedures.
main_accounts_claims: Páez portrays the directorate as a body for institutional coordination, logistics, training, equipment, statistics and processing financial documentation, while operational planning and command remained with brigades and local GAULA commanders. He describes regular kidnapping and extortion reporting, investment in vehicles and technology, and coordination with prosecutors. He distinguishes rewards from payments for information through reserved expenditure, explaining certifications, accounting review and DAS participation intended to document disbursements. He says the directorate checked paperwork rather than knowing every informant or reconstructing each field operation. Judicial questioning confronts his denial of comparative operational analysis with an April 2007 letter bearing his signature, ranking GAULA results and congratulating units for combat deaths. After initial uncertainty, he accepts the signature and says the document sought greater effort, not killing unlawfully; he cannot explain the displayed points system. He denies receiving indications at the time that units were committing unlawful killings and describes them as a tragedy when subsequently known. He also denies writing performance evaluations for local GAULA commanders. Questions about controlled extortion-payment deliveries lead him to identify prosecutorial contacts who may supply the governing procedures.
stated_positions_responses: He repeatedly limits his role to administrative coordination and rejects any inference that the signed comparison letter intended crimes. The questioner clarifies that the document is being examined without presuming intent. Victims’ questions challenge how expenditure oversight, statistics, prosecutorial accompaniment and command responsibility operated in practice. Páez generally invokes formal instructions and institutional roles, acknowledging where he cannot remember or does not know.
outcome_open_questions: The sworn testimony ends at 15:07. The court will continue comparing documents and testimony, including protected archives. The ranking methodology, actual controls over informant payments and operational deliveries, and the relationship between the directorate’s communications and local practices require further evidence. No responsibility determination concerning Páez is recorded.

english_title: Casanare recognition hearing: Delta units and contested accounts
purpose: Open the public recognition hearing for Case 03's Casanare subcase and hear victims alongside former members of the Brigade 16 Delta units. The magistrates explain the findings in Auto 055 and test whether individual acknowledgments provide detailed truth.
named_people_roles: Óscar Parra Vera and Catalina Díaz Gómez preside for the JEP Recognition Chamber. Faiber Alberto Amaya Ruiz, a former squad/platoon commander; Marco Fabián García Céspedes, a former lieutenant and Delta commander; and Edwin Leonardo Toro Ramírez, a former Delta and Gaula operations commander, give accounts of their responsibility. Derly Patiño speaks as Hugo Edgar Araque's widow. Lucy Yadira Ochoa speaks as Fermín Ochoa Barrios's daughter and challenges García Céspedes's account. Jairo Ignacio Acosta represents the Public Ministry.
main_accounts_claims: The chamber presents its account of a network that killed civilians and reported them as combat deaths, explaining intelligence targeting, operational paperwork, weapons placed on victims and institutional incentives. Amaya acknowledges participation in killings and discusses Jair Tarache's death. He says intelligence material identified Jair and his father, names officers involved in transmitting information, and describes a sense of protection created by ineffective investigations. García Céspedes accepts responsibility but faces direct challenges from Lucy Ochoa over whether he knew her father and how his present account differs from earlier testimony. He admits having lied before the JEP and alleges that he received money from General Torres Escalante while detained. Toro acknowledges killings and describes orders, altered files, reporting through brigade officers and the normalization of criminal practices. The judges question the decision to treat intelligence suspicions as permission to kill. Victims connect the killings to lost childhoods, fractured families and continuing demands to restore their relatives' names.
stated_positions_responses: The three former soldiers acknowledge responsibility, while offering accounts of command influence, institutional pressures and their own choices. Lucy Ochoa rejects parts of García Céspedes's explanation and suspects concealment of others' roles. The magistrates emphasize that recognition must be detailed and tested against victims' observations and the case record.
outcome_open_questions: The hearing breaks for lunch and is scheduled to resume that afternoon. The chamber leaves contradictions in García Céspedes's accounts and questions about superior responsibility open to further corroboration. This segment records recognition and scrutiny, without determining a final sanction.

english_title: Casanare recognition hearing: DAS cooperation, civilian recruitment and Gaula commanders

Wilson Rodríguez Mimica appears as a civilian recruiter and former paramilitary member. english_title: Casanare recognition hearing: Gaula recruiters and Battalion 44 operations
purpose: Continue individual acknowledgments and victims' responses, moving from Gaula Casanare to the Ramón Nonato Pérez Infantry Battalion 44. The session examines how recruitment, execution, concealment and institutional rewards connected the participants' actions.
named_people_roles: Óscar Parra Vera and Catalina Díaz Gómez preside. Alexander González Almario was a Gaula professional soldier involved in linking recruiters to the unit. Elbert Pérez García served in the Caníbal special group and Gaula. John Alexander Florián held command roles in counter-guerrilla units and Gaula. Miguel Fernando Ramírez appears as a civilian recruiter. Wilson Salvador Burgos Jiménez was a platoon/special-group commander; Leandro Eliecer Moná Cano describes recruitment, execution and concealment roles. Victim speakers include Dania Alejandra Achagua Cediel, Margarita Arteaga and Rosa Monroy.
main_accounts_claims: González acknowledges direct killings and helping bring victims to Gaula, while describing rewards and the damage done by falsely labelling victims. Pérez acknowledges killings, torture and participation in a systematic practice; he discusses civilian guides and lists victims whose names he seeks to clear. Florián accepts responsibility for decisions to target people, intelligence collection and fabricated combat results. Ramírez acknowledges deceiving people and handing them to soldiers, describes payments and alleged pressure, and distinguishes what he knows from what happened after the handovers. Victims challenge this boundary and ask who carried out the final acts. Burgos acknowledges ordering killings and connecting operational paperwork to commanders' demands. Moná describes his part in taking people to be killed and the pursuit of permissions, congratulations and advancement. Families describe interrupted childhoods, disability-related stigma, displacement and grief that remains unresolved when bodies or explanations are missing.
stated_positions_responses: The participants acknowledge responsibility but sometimes limit their knowledge or involvement in specific events. Victims demand the full sequence of responsibility and reject euphemistic descriptions of recruitment. The judges stress corroboration and distinguish individual choices from the institutional incentives that helped normalize the crimes.
outcome_open_questions: The chamber indicates that new allegations affecting other officers will be transmitted to the appropriate JEP chamber. english_title: Néider Jesús Calderón Meléndez, 26 May 2021: private early-truth account of DAS reports and two distinct killing episodes
purpose: The SDSJ holds a private early-truth hearing concerning Calderón’s request to enter the JEP and his individual contribution to the truth about an April 2007 operation. english_title: Casanare truth and responsibility hearing: Sanabria Correa, Vargas Vega and Pinto Sarmiento

The court presents reconstructions assembled from earlier interviews, then tests them with participants and victims.
named_people_roles: Carlos Alberto Suárez López presides, assisted by Mónica Marcela Vega Vega. Principal former military participants include operations-office sergeant Jairo Alonso Perdomo Rincón, soldiers Julio César Sierra, José Abel Pedraza Amaya and Fernando Barrera Cachay, intelligence member Hugo Gabriel Guzmán Pístala, commander Ricardo Antonio López Sánchez, and Captain Frances Orlando Reyes Rodríguez. main_accounts_claims: The morning reconstruction concerns Ander Alfonso Sanabria Correa, killed on 14 January 2007. Sierra describes collecting him under a paid-work pretext, concealing his military status and delivering him to a staged checkpoint. The court’s account assigns shooting, security and scene-alteration roles to different soldiers; Perdomo acknowledges failures in the operations paperwork and verification process while distinguishing that role from physical execution. A second event concerns William José Vargas Vega, killed on 20 October 2007. The court reconstructs intelligence personnel’s recruitment of a victim to satisfy operational demands, a false checkpoint, a killing carried out by professional soldiers, and the allocation of the reported result to another platoon. The court also discusses contributions to the Caminos de la Memoria memorial project.

english_title: Casanare truth and responsibility hearing: Fonseca Pesca, Tinjacá Pérez and Llano Arias
purpose: Second day of the August 2025 SDSJ hearings, testing reconstructed accounts of three killings and participants’ individual responsibility. The court hears former soldiers alongside relatives, with particular attention to recruitment, detention, shooting, false reports and contradictions remaining after earlier testimony.
named_people_roles: Carlos Alberto Suárez López presides with auxiliary magistrate Mónica Marcela Vega Vega. Jesús Antonio Zea, Julio César Sierra, Jenner Cuéllar Guzmán, Héctor Augusto Montoya Montoya, William Mojica Ladino and other former soldiers address their respective roles. Jairo Alonso Perdomo Rincón discusses operations paperwork; José Alejandro López Espinosa addresses command responsibility. Mauricio Tinjacá Pérez speaks as Olimpo Hernando’s brother, and the victim’s son contributes a personal portrait. John Alexander Vélez Llano appears as José Rubiel Llano’s nephew. Sergio Alejandro Toquica represents victims; Laura Virginia Benedetti participates for the Public Ministry.
main_accounts_claims: For Yesid Fonseca Pesca’s February 2007 killing, the court describes a supposed guide brought to the unit, taken to a prepared site and killed to produce an operational result. Zea admits firing and explains that other soldiers illuminated the victim because it was dark. The reconstructed account distinguishes actual participants from several soldiers named in the ordinary investigation who were reportedly assigned elsewhere. For Olimpo Hernando Tinjacá Pérez, participants describe detention under a document-check pretext, confinement at the DAS premises, a planned killing around New Year, staged combat, destruction of identifying belongings and an operations order giving apparent legality. His brother disputes the consistency of this story with earlier accounts and the family’s information about police detention, and questions the additional shots. The third event concerns José Rubiel Llano Arias. The court reconstructs an informant-assisted detention, a warning that the wrong person had been seized, a refusal to release him, a shooting and the planting of a weapon and drugs. Reading an earlier judicial analysis, it connects this killing to persecution on gender grounds. Participants acknowledge responsibility and publicly reject the characterization of Llano as a criminal.
stated_positions_responses: The families seek more than a repeated general admission: they ask who held their relatives, who shot, why accounts differ and whether higher-level instructions will be disclosed. Participants describe different degrees of knowledge and involvement, including paperwork, custody, security and execution. Their statements are not treated as interchangeable admissions to every act.
outcome_open_questions: The court reserves subsequent decisions on legal situations. The Public Ministry urges further examination of records and wound trajectories in response to relatives’ questions, stressing that truth contributions can continue after the hearing. The session closes at 19:31 and resumes on 15 August. The transcript does not settle all contradictions raised by the families.

english_title: Casanare truth hearing: the killings of Raúl Gutiérrez Perdomo and Saúl Céspedes Gutiérrez
purpose: Final day of the August 2025 SDSJ hearings, focused on the killing and false combat presentation of two young men after a political campaign event in September 2007. The hearing tests individual roles and hears the family’s objections to a newly expanded account.
named_people_roles: Carlos Alberto Suárez López presides with Mónica Marcela Vega Vega. Óscar Edmundo Gaviria Pachajoa was commander of Detonador 3; Jefferson Méndez Quintana and Óscar Mauricio Ruiz Sánchez also appear. It attributes shooting to García and Barrera, scene alteration to other soldiers, and reporting and security functions to the receiving platoon. english_title: Germán Alberto León Durán: first day of the restorative hearing following late acknowledgment
purpose: A restorative hearing following León Durán’s change from denial to acknowledgment of responsibility. The session presents his account, hears victims’ demands and begins defining truth, search, dignity and non-repetition commitments that could inform a later sanction.
named_people_roles: Germán Alberto León Durán is the retired lieutenant colonel who commanded Infantry Battalion 44 from December 2005 to November 2006. Gustavo Salazar directs the hearing; María del Pilar Valencia García and Reinere de los Ángeles Jaramillo participate in the judicial panel. Rocío del Pilar Bonilla Líbano is identified as León Durán’s lawyer. Victim voices include survivor Siervo Fernández Cuervo, Kevin Giovanni Córdoba Arias, Ana Rita Leguizamón, Nancy Sierra Ramos and Diana Contreras, speaking about their own harm or relatives including Bautista Leguizamón and Héctor Elí Contreras.
main_accounts_claims: León Durán publicly accepts responsibility for the charged killings and disappearances during his command, describing participation in an organized criminal structure rather than merely an unfortunate operational outcome. He says pressure from brigade commander Henry William Torres Escalante led him to restore the special platoon renamed Argos, permit autonomous movements, accept false intelligence and sign orders that enabled killings. He acknowledges that obedience and fear of losing command do not excuse his conduct. He lists incidents and victims, recognizes broader harm from intimidation, stigma and family displacement, and attributes his late change of position partly to discussions with his own family and encounters with victims. He delivers operational files that he says can expose alterations and identify further participants. Victims describe continuing disappearance, searches, shattered family lives and public stigma. They demand bodies, fuller accounts, other responsible people’s appearance and public correction of false accusations. Victims’ counsel welcomes the acknowledgment but challenges the continuing suggestion that his function was mainly administrative or that lack of direct presence explains gaps in knowledge.
stated_positions_responses: León Durán promises further disclosure, cooperation with the search unit, attendance at territorial acknowledgment events, memorial plaques with victims’ histories and educational talks to military trainees. He says details of individual executions require accounts from those present. Victims’ representatives request concrete, verifiable commitments, individual apologies and fuller explanation of command practices; forgiveness is not treated as unanimous or automatic.
outcome_open_questions: The judge orders the delivered records digitized, incorporated and transmitted to relevant JEP bodies. Work on a restorative agreement continues the following day. Questions remain about individual events, additional participants, missing bodies and how much the acknowledgment explains active command responsibility. This session does not impose a final sentence.

english_title: Germán Alberto León Durán: victims’ challenges and proposed restorative commitments, day two
purpose: Continuation of the late-acknowledgment restorative hearing, giving the remaining victims and counsel an opportunity to challenge León Durán’s account and formulate concrete commitments. The closing consolidates parameters for an agreement, with implementation and sentencing still to follow.
named_people_roles: Germán Alberto León Durán is the former Battalion 44 commander acknowledging responsibility. Gustavo Salazar directs the session, with other judges of the section dealing with absence of acknowledgment. Carolina Castro Mojica speaks about her husband William Salamanca; Blanca Nubia Díaz, Nancy Herrera Beltrán and Daniel Alejandro Wilkin also describe family losses. Nancy speaks about her brother José Manuel, whose surname varies in the transcript. Gerardo Hernández Hurtado represents Juan Carlos García’s relatives. Juan Pablo Ramos, of the Committee in Solidarity with Political Prisoners, presents a joint victims’ submission.
main_accounts_claims: Victims press León Durán to acknowledge responsibility without treating superior orders, paperwork or absence from execution sites as excuses. Carolina Castro asks for detailed truth about William Salamanca, other participants and the destruction of trust in the army. Other relatives describe years of searching, relatives who died without answers, threats after complaints, and the need to clear victims’ names publicly. Allegations about other institutions’ involvement are presented as their demands for investigation, not resolved findings. Counsel Ramos argues that León Durán’s account still explains omission more fully than active leadership and coordination, despite formally accepting both. He seeks the highest available sanction on the basis of what he considers an incomplete acknowledgment, while supporting joint truth sessions, searches and memorial measures. León Durán responds that he accepts both action and omission, acknowledges allocating functions within Argos, and commits to confronting his former subordinates in shared hearings. He supports search cooperation, appearances as a witness, public acknowledgment in affected municipalities, memorial histories developed with families and education for military personnel.
stated_positions_responses: The session preserves different victim positions on forgiveness and satisfaction. Counsel and the Public Ministry support concrete restorative work while asking for verification, coordination between JEP bodies and avoidance of duplicated memorial projects. The judge emphasizes that victims’ dignity and innocence must be affirmed and that the process should continue beyond the public hearing.
outcome_open_questions: At closing, the judge outlines commitments concerning truth and records, missing-person searches, collective clarification, public and individual acknowledgment, memorials and non-repetition education. He refers to additional victims and harms beyond the original charges. These are parameters for a continuing agreement and a later alternative sanction, not a completed sentence or a finding that every truth demand has been met. The hearing ends at 18:00.

english_title: Helbert Pérez García — protective-measures hearing, 6 December 2019
purpose: To assess Pérez’s reported security situation and request for temporary departure from Colombia, while considering how protection measures could remain compatible with his obligations to contribute truth, attend proceedings and take part in restorative work.
named_people_roles: Magistrate Óscar Parra Vera conducts the hearing. Pérez is the person seeking protection, supported by defence lawyer Jimmy Fernando Niño Torres. Samuel Serrano Galvis appears as the UIA prosecutor leading protection of victims, witnesses and other participants; Carlos Hernando Romero Pinzón presents the risk assessment as a UIA investigator. main_accounts_claims: Pérez says repeated threats and approaches have prevented stable family and working life despite protection already provided. He seeks permission to live abroad temporarily and promises to return when summoned rather than abandon his contribution to truth. His lawyer supports the request and asks that periodic reporting cease to require attendance before a military authority. The UIA explains that its programme protects both physical safety and continued participation in proceedings. It reports an extraordinary risk assessment and measures already adopted, with a relocation component still being implemented. Its investigator recounts reported approaches to family members and an alleged assault as part of the assessment. The Public Ministry treats the risks as serious and also asks what Pérez can contribute to identifying their origin. Parra explains that the full chamber must decide the request. He sets out unresolved questions about corroborating Pérez’s testimony, victims’ participation and how restorative duties might operate if security concerns prevent ordinary travel, collective work or residence in Colombia.

Counsel argues that nominal liberty has not translated into a stable life. outcome_open_questions: Participants are given fifteen working days to submit written proposals, subject to explaining any need for more time. Parra will refer the matter to the full chamber; urgent new risks should still be reported immediately to the UIA. The separate voluntary-statement hearing follows.
